title: The Trumpet of Truth and the Judgment of the Lord
english: The powers working these things are Jacob, who flutters the mentioned stalk; and Israel, having become higher than all toil through purity of mind, who approaches God. Since he who struggles against the mentioned opponents has need of God's mercy, but he who is unhearing of the truth is said to remember God in harmony with the things foretold, [mentioning] His mercy to Jacob and His truth to Israel.

And in Jeremiah, he who is beginning in the virtue of mercy, it is necessary, as the one speaking of God says to the God-fearing: 'Remember the mercy of your youth and the perfection of your love' (Jer 46:11); for he who is beginning in mercy, as also he who is led toward perfection in love, is able to say, 'There is the truth of Christ in me.' And as truth is appropriate for those with insight, the Savior says to the two hundred Jews who had believed in him: 'If you remain in my word, you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free' (John 8:31-32).

From the occurrence of the prophecy saying, 'All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship before him' (Ps 97:3c), it shall be said, 'All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.' For the gospel having been preached in all [that is] under heaven and in all the inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, according to the oracle of Christ, all the ends of the earth [shall see] Christ, the salvation of God.

And those who do not see [him] by [mere] sight, but with faithful assent to his teaching through which a vision is present; but also toward the intellect, those having passed through the earth and having become higher than it, not thinking of material and earthly things, but seeking and caring for the things above—the ends of the earth—those see salvation and the God who is the cause of it, the salvation of God.

All the earth, that is to say, all people upon the earth, commands a triumphal hymn to be sent up to the Lord, who brings down the invisible enemies of men, the devil and his attendants (Ps 97:4-5). And all those upon the earth, shouting to him, let them sing to him and with the lyre. But what is the lyre, as I have often said, and what is to sing in it, what it is in practice through the body...

To work the things of virtue through all the powers of the soul. And those who, plucking with this harp and uttering a song, receive a command, it is not the voice of a psalm, but rather the contemplation concerning the practical matters, instead of that which is struck upon the psalm through the instrument and some voice singing.

They blow trumpets in elms, brightly and with fire proclaiming the word of truth (Ps 97:6a). For they are not sufficient to truly awaken for a spiritual feast, saying, 'Our sufficiency is from God,' who also made us sufficient as ministers of the new covenant, who alone are able to utter this, enriching with every word and all knowledge. But those who fight against the word blow with the horn, being able against sophisms and deceptive words. And if an interpreter of divine instruction stands, he uses a trumpet of elm to utter words pedagogically and demonstratively, but he constrains the opponents of the truth with a horn.

And those divided by wisdom and by conduct, who having profited through the height of faith, rejoice, not being guilty of the judgment which the Lord came to perform (Ps 97:8b). For the Lord says, 'He who believes in me shall not be judged' (cf. John 3:18), that is, he is not subject to accusations, but stands at the step of Christ to receive the promised good things. And judging the inhabited world in righteousness, he will judge with uprightness those who have been made his own as his people, since the peoples have a straight heart and straight deeds; for he will render to each according to his deed (Ps 98:2).

Previously in Zion, according to the gift of the law and the prophets, the Lord is great, but he is so much higher than all the peoples coming from the nations through faith (Ps 97:7). For glory and honor and peace belong to everyone who works the good, first to the Jew and also to the Greek; for having been lifted up from the earth, he has drawn all to himself. Both the high and the great exist according to his nature. For he dwells in the high places, and he is great and exceedingly praiseworthy, while the generated nature is lowly and brief, and rather nothing in comparison to him. We have a vision of his highness, we who think of the things above; but also, proclaiming great things about him, we contemplate his magnitude. But not the...

title: Divine Judgment and the Worship of the Lord
english: We do not perceive greatness in terms of height sensorially

God makes all evil things a judgment that examines, and he performs the matters of truth with righteousness. Indeed, the law of justice may reveal the virtue of practical action, and the judgment may be the examination of dogmas; and what is called judgment, by which it is distinguished what is to be thought and not to be thought, and what is to be done and not to be done, he himself called justice, namely the activity according to virtue. For God does both, that is, he grants to the practical and the ascetic one the meaning of the good through the analogy of James.

You make him high, not by lifting him from below into the above (for this is a matter of bodies) [Ps 98:5], but having high and super-abundant thoughts concerning him. But the flesh received may be his footstool. Since we do not take up the things concerning the Word of God as concerning the only-begotten Son of God, we exalt the Lord God; but also considering the economy according to his sojourn, we worship the footstool of his feet, on account of him who rested upon it his motive powers, more allegorically called feet. And the ancient temple is also called his footstool, as it is written in Jeremiah: 'How the Lord in his wrath darkened the daughter of Zion! He cast down to the earth her sanctuary; he did not remember his footstool' (Lam 2:1).

To worship truly and principally it is fitting for the Trinity alone; for 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him alone shall you serve' [Deut 6:13]. According to this meaning of worship, the Lord Jesus is also worshipped: 'For all the angels of God shall worship him' [Matt 4:10]. But in another way, for the sake of honor, men are said to worship those in eminence according to this Scripture. For it is often recorded that many worshiped king David, and also the other kings of Israel.

These things are said not only concerning these men, but also concerning all those who have the same virtue as they [Ps 98:6]. And if this is truth, stand upon that which is written in Ezekiel; and it happened that the prophet was during the time of the captivity. For it is written in that Ezekiel, with God saying in the threats against Israel: 'If I bring a sword upon the earth, and they be found upon it [...].'

title: The Ascent of the Mind through Hymns to God
english: Noah, Job, and Daniel: the sword shall not enter upon them, even though the memory of men was made many thousands of years before. For Noah existed before the flood, and Job was the fifth from Abraham, many years before the prophecy. Do we not have something to say about these, or how he named those having the same virtues homonymously with them? If it is not so, it is clear that all the faithful servants also become according to Moses, and similarly regarding the others.

In a pillar of cloud he spoke to them (Ps 98:7). And from this we learn according to the writing the so-called collective manner, which names many things by the thing approaching in part, as he announces concerning all. Only to Moses, having spoken in a pillar of cloud, does he now speak concerning all. And you will find also in the Epistle to the Hebrews a pattern of such a narrative. For having enumerated all those who were well-pleasing through faith, he tells the deeds or passions of each in a collective way concerning all: 'They were struck, they were stoned,' and the following.

But what does it mean to speak of God in a pillar of cloud? This is clearly to be understood. Not because, since the word of God is firm and unswerving, it is rightly called a pillar as the church that received him is a pillar and foundation of truth; but because it is also a drinkable and fruit-bearing thing, coming like a rain unto the minds of men, it is a pillar of cloud. Perhaps through this the descent of the Savior to this place was also foretold, by which, having mounted a hollow cloud, he came into Egypt, or into the place regarding the land of a perfect man having all the virtues and guarding all the testimonies and commands of God.

To go out from the presence of the Lord God is contrary to entering before [Him] (Ps 99:2b). So then, having gone out from the presence of the Lord God, Cain did not leave a place in which the face of God was, but having become a desert of right notions concerning God in another place, he departed from His face, having embraced carelessness and atheism, as if he no longer had a vision or a thought of the appearance of God; so then, to enter before the Lord is to consider Him present through thought.

For having observed the Creator through the greatness and beauty of creations, the whole world has ascended into the thought concerning God, as if to stand before the Lord at all times, according to the saying, 'The Lord of powers lives; I stood before him' (Ps 99:4).

The gates of the Lord are the virtues through which, and in other things it is said, 'Open to me the gates of righteousness' (Ps 100:4), so that having surpassed his gates, having entered into the courts of God through theological hymns, they will gratefully confess to God.

Now he softens and restrains the passions of the listeners through the hymn, praising God the judge of men through deeds; and since his judgment is precise, examining not only the manifest things but also the hidden things of the heart, he brings it along with a kind intention. For if he were to observe according to the worth of our works, words, and intentions, we would perish utterly; but if this does not happen, he shows mercy before the judgment; for if you, Lord, should observe iniquity, who could stand? But since atonement is with you (for you are a source of goodness and mercy), we take courage that we shall obtain salvation from you, who examine what concerns us with mercy and judgment.

But for the one living rightly and desiring to have an unblemished path, it is not only the practice that ought to be blameless, but also the understanding and the knowledge regarding the doctrines, having been made precise. For someone sings, striking the instrument thoroughly and harmoniously, just as the body is, as it has been said many times, in order to produce excellent activities. And he takes up understanding, thinking about those who are prudent. And since the end of acting unblemished and thinking is to receive the presence of God into the mind and the intellect, the 'When will you come to me?' (Ps 100:2) immediately led the soul there; for your 'coming to me and dwelling as in a holy temple' (Ps 100:2) makes the aforementioned things established for me. And it will be said also to those who previously proclaimed the presence of the Savior here, 'We have sung, we have understood the things established concerning your coming into life.'
Of those who wander according to the activities of the mind, which move with evil alongside you, they become outside themselves, being passionately affected by the sensible things.
